findings.description: URL injection vulnerability: Transcript ID interpolated directly into URL string without sanitization. Pattern: URL(string: "https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript/\(id)"). Attackers could inject path traversal or query parameters via malicious transcript ID.
findings.remediation: Use URLComponents with percent encoding: var components = URLComponents(string: "https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript"); components?.path = "/" + id.addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters: .urlPathAllowed); guard let pollURL = components?.url else { throw TranscriptionError.invalidTranscriptID }

findings.description: URL injection vulnerability: Transcript ID directly interpolated into URL. Same pattern as AssemblyAITranscriptionService. No input validation on 'id' parameter.
findings.remediation: Replace string interpolation with URLComponents and percent-encode the id parameter before appending to path

findings.description: URL injection via string concatenation: baseURL and filename concatenated without validation. Pattern: URL(string: "\(baseURL)/\(filename)"). Could allow path traversal if filename contains '../' or malicious characters.
findings.remediation: Use URL.appendingPathComponent() or URLComponents: let base = URL(string: baseURL); guard let url = base?.appendingPathComponent(filename) else { throw ModelDownloadError.invalidURL }

findings.description: API key exposure via plain String: API key returned as String from Keychain, can appear in memory dumps and crash logs. No SecureString wrapper with encrypted memory storage.
findings.remediation: Implement SecureString wrapper: struct SecureString { private var encryptedData: Data; func withDecryptedValue<T>(_ action: (String) throws -> T) rethrows -> T; func clear() }. Use SecRandomCopyBytes for encryption key.

findings.description: API key property exposes plain String: apiKey property returns String? which remains in memory until garbage collected. Keychain retrieval decrypts to plain text.
findings.remediation: Replace String? return type with SecureString that stores encrypted and provides withSecureAccess pattern: public func withAPIKey<T>(_ action: (String?) throws -> T) rethrows -> T

findings.description: API key stored as plain String property: private let apiKey: String stores API key in plain memory that can be extracted from memory dumps.
findings.remediation: Use SecureString wrapper with encrypted memory storage: private let apiKey: SecureString. Implement explicit cleanup in deinit.

findings.description: Force unwrapped URL: URL(string: "https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript?limit=1")! - Hardcoded URL but force unwrap is anti-pattern that could crash if URL becomes invalid through future changes.
findings.remediation: Use guard let: guard let url = URL(string: "https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript?limit=1") else { throw TranscriptionError.invalidURL }

findings.description: Force unwrapped URL for upload endpoint: URL(string: "https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/upload")! - Same anti-pattern, could crash on initialization.
findings.remediation: Replace with guard let or use a static let with lazy initialization that throws proper error

findings.description: Force unwrapped URL for transcript endpoint: URL(string: "https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript")! - Hardcoded but unsafe unwrap.
findings.remediation: Use static constants with proper error handling or enum-based URL construction

findings.description: Force unwrapped URL in API endpoint: URL(string: "https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript?limit=1")! - Multiple force unwraps in same file.
findings.remediation: Consolidate URL construction to single method with proper error handling

findings.description: Force unwrapped URL for upload: URL(string: "https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/upload")! - Pattern repeated across multiple files.
findings.remediation: Centralize URL definitions in configuration with validation

findings.description: Force unwrapped URL for transcript creation: URL(string: "https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript")! - Same issue as other endpoints.
findings.remediation: Create URL factory or configuration object with validated URLs
